Reproducible Research: Data Quality & Analysis of Synthetic Sleep and Wellbeing Data

Reproducible Research Pipeline (synthetic demonstration)

2026-10-14

All data in this report is SYNTHETIC and fictional. It was generated by R/generate_data.R for the sole purpose of demonstrating a reproducible data-quality and analysis workflow. It does not describe real people and must not be interpreted as empirical evidence about sleep or wellbeing.

1 Introduction

This report demonstrates a fully reproducible data-analysis workflow in R. We take a deliberately messy synthetic dataset of hypothetical sleep patterns and self-reported wellbeing, validate its quality, clean it with transparent and documented functions, and then produce descriptive statistics, frequency tables, correlations and publication-style figures.

2 Methodology

The workflow is organised as independent, testable R functions:

  • Generation (R/generate_data.R) — creates a reproducible synthetic dataset (set.seed(42)) in which wellbeing genuinely depends on sleep, stress, exercise and caffeine, and then injects realistic data-quality problems (missing values, duplicates, inconsistent labels, impossible values).
  • Validation (R/validate.R) — inspects the raw data without modifying it: missing values, exact duplicates, out-of-range entries and inconsistent category labels.
  • Cleaning (R/clean.R) — operates on a copy of the raw data (the original is always preserved), standardises missingness, coerces numeric columns, nulls impossible values, canonicalises categories and removes duplicate rows.
  • Analysis (R/analysis.R) — descriptive statistics, janitor::tabyl frequency tables and Pearson correlations with hypothesis tests.
  • Figures (R/figures.R) — ggplot2 publication-style graphics.
  • Tests (tests/testthat/) — automated testthat tests on tiny datasets with known expected results.

4 Limitations

  • The data is entirely synthetic. Relationships shown here were built into the data-generating process by construction; they are not evidence about real human sleep or wellbeing.
  • Cleaning decisions (valid ranges, label mappings) are explicit assumptions defined in R/clean.R; different assumptions would yield different results.
  • Invalid and missing values are set to NA rather than imputed, so analyses use pairwise-complete observations and sample sizes vary across correlations.
  • Correlation does not imply causation; no causal claims are made.
  • No real participants, institutions, supervisors or publications are involved.
